title: Colla Health notifies patients of Cancer Care Specialists after data taken from its Metabase application
date_note: Date of Colla Health's notice letter and media notice (16 November 2026), filed with the California Attorney General. The register lists the breach date as 9 August 2026; the letter says Colla Health became aware on or around 18 August 2026.
geo_basis: headquarters as stated in the notice (8080 Westpark Dr., Houston, TX)
summary: Colla Health's notice, filed with the California Attorney General, says that on or around August 18, 2026 it learned an unauthorized party had accessed Metabase, a third-party application it uses, whose maker announced a previously unknown vulnerability. A forensic investigation found evidence that certain data may have been taken. Patients of its partner Cancer Care Specialists are being notified; names and other personal or health information may be involved.
plain: A health data company says someone got into a software tool it uses and may have taken patient information from a cancer care partner. It is offering free credit monitoring.
exec: Patient health data held by a healthcare vendor was exposed through a flaw in a third-party analytics application; third-party software risk for providers.
action: Colla Health's notice urges recipients to enroll in its 12-month credit monitoring within 90 days, review account statements and monitor credit reports; questions go to 888-213-4555.
impact: Current or former patients of Cancer Care Specialists; the notice gives no total number of people.

sources.name: Colla Health notice of data breach, 16 November 2026 (California Attorney General file)
California Attorney General breach listing: Colla Health, Inc.

validation.note: Primary: Colla Health's own notice letter, read in full from the California Attorney General's register. The notice names no attacker and no CVE for the Metabase vulnerability.

report.note: Notice letter read in full (4 pages); data types partly redacted in the sample.
